oss_reference: lssfau/walberla apps/benchmarks/PhaseFieldAllenCahn (oss_solutions.id=363, tag phase-field-allen-cahn-d3q15-d3q19); formulation read from the installed lbmpy (the library waLBerla calls)
decision: Adopt, or reject, the waLBerla two-lattice Allen-Cahn scheme (D3Q15 phase field in phi in [0,1] + D3Q19 hydro with the split pressure/viscous/surface-tension force) as TensorLBM's coupled Allen-Cahn formulation, and fix the parameter mapping between the two conventions.
alternatives: A1: keep the shipped TensorLBM stepper as is (psi in [-1,1], seven-point laplacian, D3Q19 AC+hydro populations, Korteweg force mu grad psi, Guo forcing)
A2: port the OSS formulation verbatim (D3Q15 AC lattice, lbmpy isotropic FD operators, split force, interface-tracking force, omega_phi = 1/(0.5+3M))
A3: port the OSS free-energy normalisation (beta = 12 sigma/W, kappa = 3/2 sigma W, phi in [0,1], tanh(2s/W) profile) but keep TensorLBM's data layout and explicit FD kernel
hypothesis: H1: the two formulations are the same continuum Allen-Cahn/mean-curvature model, so on one configuration the curvature-driven shrinkage of a sphere obeys dR^2/dt = -4 M sigma for both, and the two arms agree within 15%. H2: the OSS and TensorLBM interface-force normal integrals both reproduce the Laplace value sigma K = 2 sigma/R within 15%. H3 (found during work): the two conventions do NOT share the label W - the OSS profile is tanh(2s/W), TensorLBM's is tanh(s/W), so W_OSS = 2 W_TensorLBM for the same physical thickness.

metrics.primary: M2 curvature-driven shrinkage: D_eff := -(1/4) d(R^2)/dt from a linear fit of R^2(t), R from the enclosed volume of a sphere; gate |D_eff - M sigma|/(M sigma) <= 15% per arm and |D_A - D_B|/|D_B| <= 15%
secondary: M1 equilibrium interface thickness on a planar interface after 300 steps vs the arm's own analytic profile width (5%)
M3 normal line integral of the interface force through a static sphere vs sigma K = 2 sigma/R (Laplace, 15%)
diagnostics: selftest: lbmpy operator reconstruction residual must be exactly 0

baseline_control: analytic sharp-interface Allen-Cahn law v_n = -M sigma K, i.e. dR^2/dt = -4 M sigma (no free parameters: M = 0.2, sigma = 0.02 => D_analytic = 4.0e-3); static sphere is the exact control for M3
stopping_rule: each arm runs a fixed 1200 steps (900 for the coarse row); no convergence-based stopping, because the metric is a linear fit and the run length is part of the design

controlled: sphere initial condition with the arm's own equilibrium profile
same analytic target for every row
confounders: periodic images of the sphere in a 64^3 box (R0/halfbox = 0.375) slow the shrinkage slightly
the two arms use different interface thickness for the same W label (factor 2) - hence the label-W rows are not thickness matched
the OSS AC step's Guo source carries (1 - omega_phi/2); the exact force model used by the walberla app could not be read offline

repetition_rationale: deterministic problem (no seeds); repeats are the two sweeps (W, resolution) and the two arms
analysis: per row err = 100*(D_eff - M sigma)/(M sigma); aggregate = per-arm max |err| over the sweep, plus A-vs-B difference; sensitivity points = W and resolution
safety_resource_limits: each config < 200 s on one core, whole driver < 30 min single process (below the 10 min cluster threshold it is kept local; no node pinning)
interpretation_limits: static/quasi-static regime only; dynamic (Cox-Voinov) wetting and the D3Q19 hydrodynamics at 1000:1 density ratio are out of scope this round
the 15% gate applies to D_eff, not to local field errors
the OSS C++ runtime was not available (no network); the OSS arm is the lbmpy formulation executed in numpy/torch, not the walberla binary
